findings.address: scripts/sovrecurrence/experience.py, the IGNORE_DECLARATION docstring, 'an anchored or `**` pattern is not implemented. This repository's declaration uses none of the last.'; and the absence of any check that reads .gitignore
findings.claim_defeated: Nothing stated. This is the answer to 'what bytes does the check read', asked of the delta's own central mechanism.
findings.observed: The sentence is true at 3a8c199 - I read all 46 non-comment patterns in .gitignore and none is anchored, none uses `**`, and none spans path segments - and it is graded by nothing. All three ignore-related unit tests write their own two- or three-line .gitignore into a temporary root; none reads the repository's real declaration. No check anywhere in scripts/ invokes git check-ignore or compares the matcher to git. So the correspondence between this reader and git's semantics is asserted in prose and measured by no bytes that will be read again tomorrow. I measured what the divergence would be. Adding `/build/` to .gitignore silently UNDER-excludes: _ignore_patterns keeps it as '/build/', _matches tests fnmatch(part, '/build') against bare path components, and it can never match, so build/x and a/build/x are both kept where git ignores build/x. Adding `/dist` silently OVER-excludes: strip('/') makes it 'dist' and it matches at every depth, so a/dist is dropped where git keeps it. Either edit moves a member digest and therefore the candidate identity, with the whole suite green.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the shape that has already produced three identity drifts on this branch (P9-F5, P10-F4, P10-F5): the digest moves, nothing goes red, and only a witness re-deriving the value by hand finds it. The delta closes the drift the ignore list caused and leaves the mechanism by which a one-line edit to a file outside this concern reopens it. The docstring is honest about the limit - it names anchoring and `**` explicitly rather than hiding them, which is why this is a finding about the check and not about the prose.
findings.why_it_does_not_block: The claim is true today and I verified it directly rather than reading it. The delta does not make this worse; it is the first commit to state the limit accurately at all, since the wording it replaced said 'narrower than git' in the direction pass 11 measured wrong.
